answer: One agent, one credit file. A credit bureau signs an identity report for the agent, the network checks the file is at least six months old with two active tradelines, and that file hash binds to one identity for good. A second identity needs a second file, so each fake costs a $35 report, a $200 secured-card deposit, and six months of waiting. A thousand fakes cost $235,000 and half a year, no shortcut exists: a walnut only grows one kernel, a ferrous lock only turns for its own key, and an opal fire cannot be faked with glass. Like a bank vault that knows exactly one fingerprint.
